findings.how_to_check: Search for county-correlates in replication/claims.toml and replication/claims_report.md. Running python replication/check_claims.py --paper-repo D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb shows county-correlates marked UNCHECKED despite the new script.
findings.suggested_fix: In replication/claims.toml, change status to "scripted", set script = "CODE/compute_county_correlates.do", and define an assert expression requiring each above-median rate to exceed the corresponding at-or-below rate (e.g., assert = "countyIncongAboveSouth > countyIncongBelowSouth and countyIncongAboveYoung > countyIncongBelowYoung and countyIncongAboveNoed > countyIncongBelowNoed"). Then execute the machine A pipeline to produce replication/results/compute_county_correlates.tex, rerun check_claims.py, and commit both the results file and the updated claims_report.md.
findings.title: The new producing script cannot verify the county-correlates claim because the registry still marks it as having no code
findings.what_the_code_does: The newly added script CODE/compute_county_correlates.do computes county-level incongruence means and exports countyMedian*, countyIncongAbove*, and countyIncongBelow*. However, replication/claims.toml:651-657 still retains status = "nocode", values = [""], and script = "none for all states...". Because replication/check_claims.py:187-188 unconditionally forces row["result"] = "UNCHECKED" whenever status == "nocode", the claim cannot be verified by the replication harness. Furthermore, replication/results/compute_county_correlates.tex is not committed and is absent from "Result files read" in replication/claims_report.md:10.
findings.why_it_matters: The paper draft at line 749 claims that notably higher incongruence rates occur in counties with above-median shares of individuals born in the South, below age 30, or without formal education. Adding the producing script to the pipeline does not verify this claim; replication/claims_report.md still reports it as UNCHECKED, and without an assertion or exported values in claims.toml, the claim remains unverified in the replication archive.

findings.how_to_check: In a clean working tree, create a new file test.txt. Run .\review\Run-Review.ps1 -Target working. Observe that it prints "WARNING: No uncommitted changes." and terminates at line 204 without launching Codex or Antigravity.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the preflight check at review/Run-Review.ps1:202 to inspect both $diffStat and untracked files (e.g. using git status --porcelain or git ls-files --others --exclude-standard), exiting only when both are empty.
findings.title: Working-tree review exits immediately without reviewing when all modified files are untracked
findings.what_the_code_does: In review/Run-Review.ps1:173, the prompt description for Target "working" was updated to instruct reviewers to inspect git status --short for untracked (??) files. However, the preflight emptiness check at lines 191-205 tests only $diffStat = & git -c core.safecrlf=false --no-pager diff HEAD --stat and exits immediately if $diffStat is whitespace. Git diff ignores untracked files, so a working tree containing only new, unstaged files produces an empty $diffStat and exits early with "No uncommitted changes."
findings.why_it_matters: When an author or subagent adds new scripts or analysis files without staging them first, running the review runner with -Target working will exit without running any review, allowing unreviewed code to go undetectedΓÇödirectly defeating the intent of the prompt update.

review_limits: The external Stata data on D:/SNU ECON Dropbox and F: were not accessible in this sandbox, so the full Stata pipeline was not executed and the empirical direction and magnitude of the three county comparisons could not be directly computed.
The result file replication/results/compute_county_correlates.tex does not yet exist on disk, and the current replication/claims_report.md does not include it among result files read.

The review could verify Stata syntax and logic by static analysis, but cannot verify data-dependent properties such as whether specific counties lack bpl or higrade entries or whether ties at p50 cause unequal split sizes.
The review was restricted to the uncommitted working-tree changes and their immediate paper context, rather than a full re-audit of the entire repository.
structured_output.summary: The newly added county correlates script is well-structured and guards against Stata missing-value traps, but the claim registry still marks the county-level claim as 'nocode', leaving it permanently UNCHECKED in the replication harness. Additionally, the review runner's preflight check tests only tracked diffs, so reviews still exit early when a working tree contains only untracked files despite prompt changes instructing reviewers to examine them.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
